P-gp does not influence 18F-FGD brain kinetics in animals.

the P-glycoprotein function at the blood-brain barrier does not influence the brain kinetics of 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose, a radiopharmaceutical used for positron emission imaging of brain glucose metabolism.
P-gp does not impact 18F-Fluoro-deoxyglucose (18F-Fludeoxyglucose) brain distribution and estimated brain metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of P-gp at the BBB on the kinetics of 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (18F- FDG).
P-gp and 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose (18F- FDG).
the effect of the blood-brain barrier on 18F-FGD brain uptake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P-gp is unlikely to be involved in the BBB 18F-FGD kinetics.
P-gp is not involved in the regulation of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-fluordeoxyglucose) transport across the BBB.
P-gp is not a substrate or a modulator of 18F-18F-FDG kinetics at the BBB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
18F-FGD is not a P-Glycoprotien substrate at the blood-brain-barrier and therefore P-gp inhibition does not influence 18F-FDg brain kinetics in baboons.
P-gp at the BBB is not a relevant transporter for 18F–FDG and therefore not influencing the 18F-FDGl brain kinetics.
P-gp does not affect the 18F-FDGlabeled glucose metabolism in the brain, but it can affect the uptake of 2-18F-FDG into cells in the absence of glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
18F-FGD is not a substrate for P-gp and that 18F- FDG PET brain kinetics and estimated brain glucose metabolism in vivo is independent of P-gp expression at the blood– brain barrier.
the P-glycoprotein inhibitor valspodar does not affect the uptake of 2-[18F]fluoro-2-de-oxy-d-glucose (FDG) in brain.
